character_facts: Steelhead is portrayed as ruthless, treacherous, and willing to mutilate Honorata, bargain for status, and assassinate a political opponent.
Aghnar is experienced enough to take the lead in the duel before the surrender.
Honorata is grievously harmed by Steelhead.
Oda/Honorata chooses to reunite with Aghnar in death.
The Empress appeals to Steelhead for help against the invading entities.
Don Nicanor Rosamel de Rokha is identified as President of the Troglosocialik Confederation and as the only expected opponent to Steelhead's ceremony.
continuity_links: This page explicitly recaps events from the prior installment(s), connecting the duel with Aghnar to the current political ceremony around Steelhead.
The invasion by the wall-passing vampires is linked directly to the dimensional breach caused during Steelhead's earlier battle.
dialogue_meaning: The page functions as a 'previously' recap rather than a scene of live dialogue.
It explains that Steelhead's actions during and after the duel with Aghnar led both to disaster and to his rise toward formal recognition as Supreme Metabaron.
It frames Steelhead as militarily effective but morally monstrous, emphasizing betrayal, mutilation, political murder, and opportunism.
locations: the Halerce, described as the oldest tree in the galaxy
a ceremonial or monumental interior shown in the recap illustration
lore_facts: Combat can occur in 'Metacraft' and can traverse different dimensions.
Mini-bombs can be set within bodies for suicide.
The Pthagureans are capable of collective suicide and can decree or halt it.
Cross-dimensional conflict can open breaches through which hostile entities enter the universe.
The office or title of 'Supreme Metabaron' exists.
The 'Medallion of High Nobility' is a formal distinction tied to ambassadorial approval.
Philodendra is identified as the Troglosocialik capital.
The Halerce is described as the oldest tree in the galaxy.
Millions of sweet-voiced Dyukkas sing at the Halerce.
The Troglosocialik Confederation has a president.
plot_events: Steelhead and Aghnar fight each other to the death in their separate Metacraft and move across dimensions during the battle.
Aghnar gains the advantage, and Honorata and Steelhead surrender.
At the last moment, Steelhead badly mutilates Honorata; Aghnar cannot bear it, and Steelhead is identified as cold and treacherous.
Oda/Honorata chooses to rejoin Aghnar, and the two commit suicide by detonating mini-bombs in their bodies.
Despite being despised for his methods, Steelhead is said to have saved humanity and the Pthagureans halt their collective suicide.
Vampiric entities come through walls, devour guests' brains, and include the Imperial Couple among their victims.
The Empress asks Steelhead for help; the entities are said to have entered through a breach opened by Steelhead's cross-dimensional battle with Aghnar.
Steelhead defeats the vampires and reseals the breach.
In exchange for helping, Steelhead demands the title of Supreme Metabaron and the Medallion of High Nobility, which requires the ambassadors' agreement.
To remove opposition to the ceremony, Steelhead travels to Philodendra and executes Don Nicanor Rosamel de Rokha during his morning meditation.
Steelhead then returns to the Imperial Palace to receive the honor he seeks.
